correctness.rationale: The rational quotient is invariant under rotation by the primitive qth root and consequently is a rational function of z^q. Equality of the two modulus profiles gives the reflection-pair property; zero/pole valuations then yield uniquely determined integer intervals [-b_lambda,a_lambda], with disjoint orbit factorization proving completeness. The degree count q sum(a+b)<=d proves the universal bound and an explicit product polynomial attains equality. Finite enumerations corroborate 16 examples but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: An exact all-degree classification of a natural finite-dimensional inverse problem with repeated roots is motivated by a documented rational versus irrational line-angle identifiability gap. The explicit sharp ambiguity exponent and q>d universal-injectivity threshold quantify the cost of rational resonance and supply a concrete uniqueness test for any input polynomial, without relying on a speculative downstream application.
